assign.title: Our own AI harness
assign.question: Should we build our own model-agnostic agent harness (on OpenRouter or direct provider APIs) to replace the Claude Agent SDK inside Servex, and what do we build first?

node.text: OpenRouter or direct? Feature parity across Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, xAI Grok and Groq: tools, streaming, caching, thinking, cost reporting.
OpenRouter agent package or our own harness?
The harness parts: file context, CLAUDE.md plus on-demand skills, MCP, tools and the loop, auto-compact, session ids with fork and resume, cost per turn.
Permissions and sandboxing: worktrees each with a dev server, node instead of bash for control over input and output.
How does it replace the Claude Agent SDK inside Servex (Servex/agents/) so spawning is model-agnostic?
Multi-model fleets with cross-review: several models on one task, then each checks the others.
Model switcher in the chat and dictation widget: assistant model in config, mastermind model per card.

node.text: Tools: OpenRouter normalizes tool calling to one OpenAI-style shape across providers, with parallel_tool_calls, tool_choice and streamed tool deltas; it publishes a per-model Tool Call Error Rate.
node.why: credence: established — stated in OpenRouter's own tool-calling docs, fetched 2026-09-28. Normalized shape is not the same as equal quality: the error-rate metric exists because providers differ.

node.text: Caching differs per provider even through OpenRouter: Anthropic needs explicit cache_control (writes 1.25x or 2x, reads 0.1x); OpenAI, Gemini, Grok cache automatically; Groq only on Kimi K2. Gemini uses only the last breakpoint.
node.why: credence: established — OpenRouter caching guide, 2026-09-28. So a harness still needs a per-provider cache strategy; OpenRouter passes the parameter through, it does not hide the difference. Sticky routing keeps a session on one provider for 10 minutes of inactivity.

node.text: Thinking is unified as one reasoning param (effort or max_tokens), but control is uneven: Gemini decides its own token count, some OpenAI models hide reasoning, and reasoning_details must be echoed back unmodified across tool calls.
node.why: credence: established — OpenRouter reasoning guide. The echo-back rule matters most for our loop: a harness that trims or reorders reasoning blocks between tool turns breaks the chain on Anthropic.

node.text: Cost per turn comes free: every OpenRouter response now carries usage.cost in dollars plus cached_tokens and reasoning_tokens, on the last SSE chunk when streaming. Direct APIs give tokens only; we would keep our own price table.
node.why: credence: established — OpenRouter usage-accounting page says full usage is always included and the old include flags are deprecated. This alone answers the owner's cost-visibility ask with no pricing table to maintain.

node.text: Price: OpenRouter passes provider token prices through unmarked; the cost is a 5.5% fee on credit purchases (Stripe), or with your own keys (BYOK) free up to $25k a month, then 5%.
node.why: credence: established — OpenRouter FAQ, 2026-09-28. At our scale the gateway costs about 5% or nothing; not a deciding factor.

node.text: The real cost switch is the subscription: Servex minions run on the Claude subscription today (usage windows, not dollars). Claude via OpenRouter or the direct API bills per token, which could cost far more for the same Claude work.
node.why: credence: contested — that we are on a subscription is clear from the usage-window skill; how much more per-token billing would cost is unmeasured. Measure a day of token usage before moving Claude traffic off the subscription.

node.text: Batch work is available through OpenRouter too: a Batch API at about half price on 70+ models, median batch finished in 7 minutes. Useful for cross-review fleets that need not answer live.
node.why: credence: established — OpenRouter announcement with its own beta numbers (230k batches). Discount varies by model; web-search calls bill at full rate.

node.text: The OpenRouter agent package is @openrouter/agent (TypeScript, beta; Python and Go ports): callModel loops until a stop condition (stepCountIs, hasToolCall, maxCost), runs tool() helpers, plugs in remote MCP servers, streams.
node.why: credence: established — npm page says beta; overview page lists these primitives. It is a loop library, not a Claude-Code-like product.

node.text: It lacks most of what our minions rely on: no file or shell tools, no context compaction, no session persistence or resume, no CLAUDE.md or skills loading. Those are exactly the parts the owner listed.
node.why: credence: contested — the overview page does not mention them; absence from docs is not proof of absence. Check the package source before building on this (see the question below).

node.text: Shortest path, no new harness: the Claude Agent SDK already runs against OpenRouter by setting ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN; Servex already passes a per-agent env to query().
node.why: credence: established — OpenRouter's own Claude Code guide says the Agent SDK works with the same env vars, and Agents.js spreads this.env into the SDK options. Caveat: the guide warns non-Anthropic models may not work correctly with Claude Code.

node.text: That route keeps sessions, resume, fork, compaction, skills, hooks and permissions for free, but ties every model to the Claude Code prompt and tool shapes, which other models were not tuned for.
node.why: credence: contested — the feature list is established (Agents.js options use resume, forkSession, permissionMode); how badly GPT, Gemini or Grok behave inside Claude Code prompts is unmeasured and is the whole question.

node.text: Our own harness is small in the loop and large in the edges: a tool loop is about 100 lines, but compaction, resume, permissions and MCP each took the Agent SDK real work. Build only the parts the proxy route proves broken.
node.why: credence: contested — an engineering estimate, not a measurement.

node.text: Does a non-Anthropic model (GPT, Gemini, Grok) finish a real minion brief through Claude Agent SDK + OpenRouter at a quality we would merge? One measured run per model answers the build-or-proxy question.
node.why: credence: unknown — nobody has tested it in this repo; OpenRouter only says it may not work correctly.

node.text: Recommendation: step 1 is a proxy spike, not a harness: one Servex role with env ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointed at OpenRouter and a non-Claude model, run on a real small brief. Build our own loop on @openrouter/agent only where it fails.
node.why: credence: contested — a build choice. Alternative: start our own harness now on @openrouter/agent; costs more up front, but gives prompts tuned per model. The spike costs an hour and decides between them with data.

node.text: Same-model review is biased: LLM judges favor their own outputs and their own family, and stronger models show more of it. This backs the owner's instinct that the writer should not review its own code.
node.why: credence: established — several independent papers (NeurIPS 2024 Panickssery et al.; 2604.22891 across 20 models). A fresh context helps; a different model family helps more.

node.text: Plain debate (agents argue until they agree) often loses to a simple majority vote or self-consistency, at higher cost.
node.why: credence: contested — two 2025-26 papers find this on reasoning benchmarks; other papers report gains. Benchmarks are not code review, so the transfer is uncertain.

node.text: Mixing model families is the one change that reliably helps: one study calls model heterogeneity a universal antidote for debate, and another found a mixed-model debate cut factual errors by over 30%.
node.why: credence: contested — consistent across two groups, but on QA and reasoning benchmarks, not code tasks. This is the strongest argument for OpenRouter in the fleet plan: diversity needs other providers.

node.text: Design that follows the evidence: independent drafts first (no peeking), then each reviewer from a different family checks one draft against a fixed rubric (true? logical? disputable?), then one judge picks. Not a free-form chat.
node.why: credence: contested — diversity-first plus stated confidence beat vanilla debate in 2601.19921; the rubric is the owner's three questions. Untested on our tasks.

node.text: Cost stays sane: cross-review can use the batch API at about half price when not live, and usage.cost on every reply lets a fleet stop at a maxCost ceiling.
node.why: credence: established — both features documented by OpenRouter; maxCost is a stop condition in @openrouter/agent.

node.text: Does a mixed-family review catch more real defects than a fresh same-model Opus review on OUR tasks? Needs a measured A/B on landed tasks with known bugs before fleets become the default.
node.why: credence: unknown — published gains are on benchmarks; no data on code review in this repo.

node.text: Recommendation: start with one cross-family reviewer per build task (e.g. Opus writes, GPT or Gemini reviews via OpenRouter against the three-question rubric), measure caught defects, and grow to fleets only if it pays.
node.why: credence: contested — follows from established self-preference bias plus contested debate results. Alternative: a fresh-context same-model reviewer, cheaper and on the subscription, but keeps family bias.

node.text: Recommendation: OpenRouter for every non-Claude model (one key, one shape, cost in each reply); keep Claude on the subscription via the Agent SDK until a measured token day says otherwise. Direct APIs only for a gap.
node.why: credence: contested — this is a judgment: parity is good enough for tools, streaming and cost, uneven for caching and thinking, and the subscription question is open. The alternative is all-OpenRouter including Claude, which buys uniformity at a price we have not measured.

node.text: Claude Agent SDK already supplies the full agent loop, tool execution and context management as a library -- we are not building the loop from scratch today.
node.why: credence: established -- Anthropic own docs describe query() as shipping the same loop, tools and context handling Claude Code uses.

node.text: Automatic compaction summarizes older turns and re-injects CLAUDE.md once context nears its limit; context editing (clearing stale tool results) is a separate opt-in beta, not on by default.
node.why: credence: established -- both behaviors are documented explicitly, including the beta header required for context editing.

node.text: Skills load on demand already, but only by prepending Load the X skill to the first message -- the SDK has no option to preload a skill into a top-level query() session.
node.why: credence: established -- our own code comment cites the SDK d.ts line numbers for the gap (Options.skills only filters, AgentDefinition.skills only preloads for a Task-tool subagent).

node.text: Session ids, fork and resume already work: Servex mints the uuid at spawn, query() stays open in streaming-input mode, and spawn({resume, fork}) reopens or copies a conversation.
node.why: credence: established -- described in the readme and proven by fork-proof.mjs and revive-proof.mjs in the same directory.

node.text: Per-turn cost, duration and turn count already arrive for free in the SDK result event -- no accounting code of ours computes it.
node.why: credence: established -- documented in the readme event table (type: result -> ok, cost, duration_ms, turns).

node.text: MCP tools are already wired as in-process node functions (createSdkMcpServer) rather than HTTP, so an agent tool call runs inside Servex with no round trip.
node.why: credence: established -- documented in the readme, seven agent tools plus ops.js and jobs.js built this way.

node.text: Does any OpenRouter-facing SDK or gateway offer an equivalent to automatic compaction plus CLAUDE.md re-injection, or would leaving Anthropic mean building a summarizer ourselves.
node.why: credence: unknown -- not checked; belongs with the opus scout own OpenRouter-vs-direct question but the harness parts (q2iwg) depend on the answer.

node.text: Recommendation: our own layer (skills-as-first-message, node-tool MCP, worktree fencing) sits atop a swappable model call -- only query() itself, with its compaction and caching, is SDK-specific and needs rebuilding on a switch.
node.why: credence: established -- follows from the claims above: everything except query() itself is already our own code sitting on top of the SDK.

node.text: Sandboxing today is entirely the SDK permission_mode (acceptEdits, bypassPermissions, plan) assigned per role in roles.js -- there is no OS-level jail in our own code.
node.why: credence: established -- read roles.js directly, no path or command allowlist code exists beside the SDK mode string.

node.text: Claude Code CLI adds an OS-level Bash sandbox (bubblewrap on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS) restricting writes to working or temp dirs; unconfirmed whether the Agent SDK query() we call inherits this.
node.why: credence: contested -- describes the Claude Code CLI architecture from a third-party writeup, not verified against Anthropic own SDK docs for query().

node.text: Real isolation for risky work comes from git worktrees, each on its own free port and its own dev server, never the live tree -- proven in worktree-up.mjs.
node.why: credence: established -- read the script; it allocates a free port, npm ci in isolation, and boots a private server before anything is trusted.

node.text: Do not edit outside your fence is enforced only by the minion skill prose, not by any tool -- nothing stops a Write or Edit call from landing outside the brief stated files.
node.why: credence: established -- searched tools.js and roles.js for any path-check code; none exists.

node.text: hold.mjs --paths is the one real enforced fence in this system, but it fences live-reload visibility, not the write itself -- a write outside --paths still succeeds.
node.why: credence: established -- the reload-hold section describes exactly this scope: it holds reloads, never blocks a write.

node.text: jobs.js already routes low-judgment work (read, grep, watch, check) through node instead of bash or agent judgement -- exactly the use-node-for-IO pattern the owner asked about, ready to extend.
node.why: credence: established -- read the doc; five job kinds already run through node with zero tokens spent.

node.text: Is a real path allowlist at the tool layer (reject a Write or Edit outside a glob) worth building, or does worktree isolation plus convention cover the actual risk seen so far (fence violations, not malicious escape)?
node.why: credence: unknown -- no incident in the logs so far was a malicious escape; every fence miss found was an honest agent mistake, so the cost/benefit is unverified.

node.text: Recommendation: keep worktrees as the hard boundary for anything risky, and add a cheap tool-layer path check next -- cheaper than a full OS sandbox and closes the one real gap this dig found (claim 4).
node.why: credence: established -- follows from claims 1, 3 and 4: worktrees already work, the gap is a missing cheap check, not missing isolation.

node.text: Servex/agents/ imports only three SDK functions -- query, getSessionInfo, getSessionMessages -- from @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk, all inside Agents.js.
node.why: credence: established -- read the import line directly, and grepped the whole agents/ dir for the package name.

node.text: tiers.js already has a provider field per tier (anthropic) that nothing reads yet -- the seam for a per-tier provider switch already exists in the code, just unused.
node.why: credence: established -- read tiers.js; its own top comment says moving a tier to another provider is meant to be a one-line change here.

node.text: Replacing query() means rebuilding, per provider: the streaming-input session that stays alive between turns, session-id issuance, resume and fork, and the typed result event carrying cost, turns and duration.
node.why: credence: established -- these are exactly the SDK features Agents.js depends on today, per the readme own description.

node.text: MCP tool wiring (createSdkMcpServer, mcpServers in spawn options) is also SDK-specific -- an OpenRouter-based loop would need its own tool-calling convention to keep the in-process node tools.
node.why: credence: established -- readme describes this as an SDK mechanism (Agent.door() puts it in mcpServers).

node.text: Does the OpenRouter agent package or any OpenRouter SDK expose a streaming-input, long-lived session with resume, fork and per-turn cost -- the four things query() gives us free -- or would all four need reimplementing?
node.why: credence: unknown -- out of this scouts fence (belongs with opus qgyhm), but qqtqi cannot be answered without it.

node.text: A safer first step than a full replacement: add an openrouter tier in tiers.js and a second code path in Agents.spawn() chosen by the tier provider field, so Anthropic keeps working while one low-stakes tier is tried.
node.why: credence: unknown -- a build proposal, not a checked fact; nobody has prototyped this in the repo yet.

node.text: Recommendation: do not replace the SDK -- add it as a second backend behind tiers.js existing provider field, starting with one low-stakes tier, since Agents.js queue/registry/wake/log machinery is already provider-agnostic.
node.why: credence: established -- follows from claims 1, 2 and 4: only about six SDK calls in one file need a second implementation, everything else already does not touch the SDK.

node.text: Dictate.js only does speech-to-text via whisper-server or the browser SpeechRecognition -- it has no model concept at all, and there is no model-switcher UI anywhere in ux/Dictate today.
node.why: credence: established -- grepped the whole module for model, only one unrelated comment hit.

node.text: The model the owner means for the switcher is the mastermind or manager model per card, not the transcription engine -- tiers.js already assigns a model per role server-side, with no per-card override today.
node.why: credence: established -- read both files; model is chosen by role/tier, never by card.

node.text: The assistant layer (assistant-<card>, Assistant.js) is meant to be cheap and transparent per the owner own dictated words -- the switcher belongs on the manager or mastermind tier, not the fast assistant.
node.why: credence: established -- the owner own dictation says the assistant model may stay configured separately while the mastermind model is what gets switched.

node.text: No card-level model override field exists yet in Layers.js or registry.js -- spawn_agent takes a model but nothing in the UI lets a person pick one per card before spawning.
node.why: credence: established -- grepped both files for a per-card model field; found none.

node.text: Where should the model picker actually live -- card toolbar control, a dashboard setting, or a spoken command the assistant parses (use opus for this)? The owner dictation did not say.
node.why: credence: unknown -- the owner named the need but not the placement.

node.text: Recommendation: add the picker to the card chrome next to wherever it already shows its manager name or state, writing straight to spawn_agent model field -- reuse tiers.js TIERS list as the dropdown options.
node.why: credence: established -- follows from claims 2 and 4: the model is a per-card spawn_agent argument with no existing UI, and tiers.js already lists the valid choices.

node.text: The fence check needs no new layer: the Agent SDK's canUseTool callback or a PreToolUse hook, added in Agents.js options(), can refuse Write/Edit outside the brief's globs. Bash writes still pass, so worktrees stay.
